title: Incremental region-oscillation fault harness for soft-degradation & dependency blackholes
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic chaos harness that simulates short-duration region oscillations (rapid switches between high-latency and partial blackhole), combined with progressive GPU pool exhaustion and dependency blackholes (e.g., metadata service and model-store). The harness will exercise circuit breakers, admission controls, prefix/KV cache behaviour, and load-shedding logic to validate SLO preservation and graceful degradation decisions.

Scope: orchestrate multi-region scenarios across a single control-plane region plus two serving regions (primary/secondary). Simulate: (1) flaky inter-region latency spikes (100-800ms) for 30-120s windows, (2) transient blackhole for control-plane or model-store (drop 80-100% of RPCs for 15-60s), and (3) staged GPU eviction patterns that reduce available GPUs by 10-70% over a 10m window. The harness will run deterministically (seeded) so experiments are reproducible and include a golden baseline run.

Why: Existing tests cover full region loss and large blackholes, but we lack coverage for fast oscillation patterns and compound degradations that produce tail latency and oscillatory backpressure, which are common in cloud noisy-neighbor cases. This ticket delivers tools + dashboards + runbook to validate circuit-breaker thresholds and progressive shed policies under those conditions.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable chaos harness that can be configured with: oscillation frequency, latency amplitude, blackhole probability, GPU eviction ramp and dependency targets
End-to-end test workflow that runs a golden baseline and three attack profiles (mild, medium, severe) and emits artifact JSON with metrics and traces
Dashboards (Grafana) or a dedicated Console view showing SLO attainment, p50/p95/p99 latency, token-per-second throughput, retry amplification, and circuit-breaker open/close events for each run
An ops runbook that lists recommended circuit-breaker tweaks and load-shed rules for 99.9% and 99.99% SLO targets, plus rollback guidance
One completed canary run against the staging cluster and a follow-up reading from oncall and platform leads documenting observed regressions and recommended changes
runbook: Pre-check: verify staging GPU inventory and ensure synthetic load generator has multi-region clients configured
1) Start golden baseline for 10m and capture metrics: token TPS, latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, model-store RPC error rates
2) Run mild profile: oscillation 60s period, 150-300ms inter-region latency spikes, 10% GPU eviction over 10m, model-store blackhole 10% for 20s
3) Run medium profile: oscillation 45s, 300-500ms latency spikes, 30% GPU eviction, model-store blackhole 40% for 30s
4) Run severe profile: oscillation 30s, 500-800ms latency spikes, 60% GPU eviction, control-plane blackhole 80% for 45s
5) Collect traces, circuit-breaker events, admission-control logs, and admission rejections; annotate timeline with model version and routing policy
6) Post-run: analyze and produce artifact with root-cause hypotheses, suggested mitigations, and config patches to test in next iteration
metrics_to_track: SLO attainment: success-rate per minute for 99.9% threshold
Latency: p50/p95/p99 token-latency and end-to-end request-latency
Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec per region
Retry amplification: average retries per request and retry storm incidence
Circuit-breaker events: open/close count and duration
Admission control: rejections and reasons (capacity, cost, policy)
KV cache hit ratio and cold-start rate after oscillation windows
test_plan: Unit tests for simulated network faults (deterministic scheduler + seeded RNG)
Integration: orchestrate network emulation using tc/netem in staging with container-level controls
System: run full harness for each profile with synthetic traffic that matches customer token length distribution (mix of short chat and long-completion flows)
Canary: run medium profile during off-peak on a canary deployment and monitor for false positives
Safety: automatic abort if critical thresholds hit (control-plane error-rate >10% sustained for 60s)
